subject: ClearHarbor on-prem: cluster topology, storage pathing and retention playbook
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@clearharbor.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ClearHarbor on-prem: cluster topology, storage pathing and retention playbook

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our intake call, we want to capture a compact playbook for the on-prem Kubernetes cluster you'll run with Redwood Private. Goals for this note: confirm the physical/network layout, storage binding choices (local NVMe, NVMe-oF, iSCSI, or SAN), and retention/audit constraints so we can size node pools and the KV cache strategy.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether the target racks have dual ToR fabrics (A/B) and whether the NICs on the host are 2x25G or 2x100G?
- Do you have a procurement timeline for the 1U NVMe nodes listed in your inventory sheet? (attached)
- Any regulatory retention window for logs/trace/audit (e.g., 1 year vs 7 years)?
- Are local SSDs allowed for ephemeral KV cache, or must all state be on encrypted blockstore?

Attachment: site-inventory.xlsx (basic site inventory you shared)

Proposed next steps: once we get the fabric/NIC and retention constraints we'll publish a 1-page nodeclass + PV-binding recommendation and a short runbook for attach order and emergency detaches.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0172

From: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@clearharbor.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearHarbor IT <it@clearharbor.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearHarbor on-prem: cluster topology, storage pathing and retention playbook

Hi Chloe —

Thanks, happy to confirm details. Answers inline: 
- Fabric: each rack has A/B ToR; we have 2x100G bonded ports on the hosts you flagged. The top-of-rack switches are Cumulus 4.3 and support LACP.
- NVMe nodes: procurement expected in Q4; we have a pilot set of 3 x 1U servers today (listed in the attached NVMe diagram). Those pilots are running ESXi but can be reimaged.
- Retention: for patient-adjacent telemetry we must retain audit logs for 3 years; anonymized tracing can be 1 year.
- Local SSDs: allowed for ephemeral cache only; anything classified as persistable must be on encrypted blockstore (we use vendor-managed SAN for long-term).

One caveat: our security team requires that any KV cache on local NVMe be encrypted at rest with keys pulled from our HSM; we can provide APIs for key rotation.

Attaching nvme-layout-diagram.pdf that the site team sent.

Lisa
Lisa Morgan
Head of IT Operations, ClearHarbor MedTech
lisa.morgan@clearharbor.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-08-31T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearHarbor on-prem: cluster topology, storage pathing and retention playbook

Thanks for the confirmation, Lisa — that's very helpful. I've sketched a short commercial and delivery note for the pilot and the full landing:

Commercial/delivery bullets:
- Pilot (3 nodes): field validation of nvme-local + NVMe-oF fallback. 6-week engagement for imaging, VPN handshake, KMS/HSM key exchange, and acceptance tests.
- Full landing (rackset): reserved capacity offer for dedicated pool with SLA. We'll need exact inventory before we lock pricing.

Delivery checklist for engineering (for Chloe/Aditya to validate):
- Network: configure LACP on host uplinks; plan for a redundant BGP session between ToR fabrics and the customer edge.
- Nodeclasses:
  * control-plane (3x m5-like): on separate VLAN, no GPU, small local SSD for journaling only
  * nvme-cache (pilot 3x): local NVMe encrypted with HSM keys; runtime will use KV cache with TTLs tuned to token profile
  * worker-gpu (future): isolated VF pool, separate BGP advertisement to allow traffic egress through the high-bandwidth fabric
- PV binding: prefer CSI that supports immediate binding to local NVMe for low-latency shards; fallback to NVMe-oF target over RDMA if node unavailable.
- Retention & evidence: provide an S3 export plan for audit logs to ClearHarbor archival (3-year retention) with signer metadata.

Marissa — can you confirm the pilot SLAs and whether we can provide a temporary KMS integration sandbox for the customer during the pilot?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions & Field Delivery, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@clearharbor.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearHarbor on-prem: cluster topology, storage pathing and retention playbook

Lisa / Chloe — quick tech note from the infra side, pulled from our internal runbook. Quoting relevant pieces from Lisa's email above where helpful.

> "each rack has A/B ToR; we have 2x100G bonded ports on the hosts"
- Good: we will recommend two uplink NICs per node with LACP active; plan for MTU 9k for nvme-oF RDMA to limit CPU overhead.

> "Local SSDs: allowed for ephemeral cache only; anything classified as persistable must be on encrypted blockstore"
- Implementation details: Redwood agent will mount local NVMe as ext4/xfs with dm-crypt using keys from the customer's HSM via a short-lived token. We will run a small sidecar that zeroes cache on eviction/drain to avoid stale PHI exposure.

Storage fallback pattern (pilot):
1) Primary: local NVMe (encrypted) bound via CSI-local for low-latency shard storage.
2) Fallback: NVMe-oF target served from a small SAN cluster in the same rack over RoCEv2; will rely on LACP path with ECMP.
3) Archive: nightly snapshot to the vendor SAN (s3-compatible target) with KMS envelope encryption per customer policy.

Operational checks for acceptance testing:
- KV cache TTLs must be validated with a sanity load (we'll run a synthetic token replay to ensure hit-rate targets).
- Eviction: pods should gracefully flush to NVMe-oF target when the node enters drain state (we'll test node-drain scenarios).
- Audit: ensure the s3 audit export contains signer and rotation events.

I'll prepare a short appendix for the runbook with the CSI config snippet and the dm-crypt key retrieval flow for Lisa's team to review.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
